title: ProOPF: Benchmarking and Improving LLMs for Professional-Grade Power Systems Optimization Modeling
claim: Prior work spans coarse cross-domain tasks; ours builds fine-grained within-domain data via graded levels from explicit to semantic instructions.
layout: Left-to-right grid of four levels on two axes, plus dataset bar chart
description: A wide diagram with a vertical axis running from Base OPF to Structural Extensions and a horizontal axis running from Explicit Instruction to Semantic Inference. A blue region on the left holds Levels 1 and 3, and a green region on the right holds Levels 2 and 4. Each level is a stack of modules (OPF Model ω, Structural Library S, Solver R) feeding a robot icon and a Template τ card. A central Random Sampling box lists parameter edits such as generators at bus 32 → 500 MW. The green side adds a flow that samples δk, retrieves an expert tree and produces scenario text. On the right, a human icon labelled Data Cleaning & Text Refinement sits above a bar chart for C1–C4, each bar capped at a 3K dashed line. Example instructions run along the bottom.
caption: From cross-domain to within-domain generalization in LLM-based optimization. Existing works emphasize coarse-grained generalization across heterogeneous optimization tasks, whereas ProOPF-B/D targets fine-grained, within-domain generalization in OPF through parametric and structural formulation modifications.
abstract: Growing renewable penetration introduces substantial uncertainty into power system operations, necessitating frequent adaptation of dispatch objectives and constraints and challenging expertise-intensive, near-real-time modeling workflows. Large Language Models (LLMs) provide a promising avenue for automating this process by translating natural-language (NL) operational requirements into executable optimization models via semantic reasoning and code synthesis. Yet existing LLM datasets and benchmarks for optimization modeling primarily target coarse-grained cross-domain generalization, offering limited, rigorous evaluation in power-system settings, particularly for Optimal Power Flow (OPF). We therefore introduce \textbf{ProOPF-D} and \textbf{ProOPF-B}, a dataset and benchmark for professional-grade OPF modeling: ProOPF-D contains 12K instances pairing NL requests with parameter adjustments and structural extensions to a canonical OPF, together with executable implementations; ProOPF-B provides 121 expert-annotated test cases with ground-truth code, enabling end-to-end evaluation under both concrete and abstract OPF modeling regimes.
